accuracy_note: value_bits is a canonical encoding or fixed-bit pattern; mask_bits marks fixed bits. Zero mask bits are operand-variable fields. Chimera-native encodings are project-defined. The current instruction rows are a partial catalog of verified forms, not an exhaustive enumeration of every instruction, extension, CPU model, or encoding variant. A target is compiler-supported only for forms implemented by the encoder/decoder and backend; catalog presence alone does not imply complete executable support. Internet research update 2026-10-08: additions are sourced from the official ISA specifications listed in sources; this remains a partial catalog and each encoding must be verified against the referenced architecture manual before use in an executable encoder/decoder. Inventory update 2026-10-09: added a broad architecture-family inventory covering historical, current, embedded, vector, GPU, and virtual ISAs. Rows marked catalog-only are discovery targets and have zero verified instruction forms; the inventory is intentionally not represented as literally exhaustive, and does not imply encoder, decoder, simulator, or hardware support. GPU/VM/extension entries are explicitly distinguished from general-purpose CPU base ISAs. Execution-candidate update: execution_model lists per-architecture and per-instruction candidates with encoding, mapping, compatibility, binary-format and conformance metadata. Reference-interpreter support is limited to explicitly implemented integer operations and does not imply complete native CPU execution. Update 2026-10-11: appended additional candidate architecture and extension inventory rows from the project's curated source registry. New rows with zero instruction forms are discovery/training candidates only; no encoding, decode, execution, or conformance support is implied. AI-assisted mapping must cite database row/source references and report uncertainty; only deterministic, validated backends may execute instructions. Update 2026-10-12: added explicit RV32I sample rows and a Z80 register-move sample; corrected the Power ISA ADDI worked sample to the encoding for addi r3,r4,1 (0x38640001). New instruction rows are catalogued samples, not proof of decoder/backend/conformance support. Existing compatibility mappings remain advisory unless an implementation and tests are explicitly listed. Update 2026-10-12: added explicit RV32I sample rows and a Z80 register-move sample; corrected the Power ISA ADDI worked sample to the encoding for addi r3,r4,1 (0x38640001). Added enriched cross-ISA encoding examples with byte/binary representations, affected registers/flags, memory effects, source references, compatibility requirements, and explicitly proposal-only N-bit mappings. These samples do not establish backend or conformance support. Clarification: instruction bit strings and hex_word encode the architectural instruction word. hex_bytes is a memory-order byte sequence only when the target byte order is specified; bi-endian architectures leave it null until a target endianness is selected.

research_update.method: Official vendor and standards documentation reviewed for architecture scope, instruction reference organization, and extension/version status. Curated reference supplement; not exhaustive. Candidate inventory additions recorded as catalog-only unless existing source-backed instruction forms are present; no external source is treated as proof of implementation. On 2026-10-12, checked official Intel SDM index, Arm machine-readable A64/A32/T32 instruction descriptions, the ratified RISC-V specification library, and OpenPOWER ISA 3.1c; attached per-candidate implementation plans and explicit effect-confidence labels. This remains a source-backed candidate inventory, not an exhaustive instruction import for every processor.

source_findings.finding: Intel SDM separates basic architecture, the full A–Z instruction reference, system programming (memory management, protection, interrupts/exceptions, multiprocessor, VMX/VT, SGX), and model-specific registers. Track extension and processor feature availability separately.
An ISA specifies programmer-visible instructions, formats, registers, data types, memory model, privilege, and exceptions; distinguish ISA from microarchitecture.

Track AArch64/A64 separately from AArch32 A32 and T32 (Thumb/Thumb-2); A64 is fixed 32-bit while T32 uses 16- and 32-bit encodings. Feature availability depends on architecture profile/version and implemented extensions.

RISC-V is modular: record base ISA, extensions, privileged architecture, and ratification status independently. Compressed C instructions use 16-bit encodings; base instructions commonly use 32 bits. The ratified library contains extensions beyond M/A/F/D/C/V.
Power ISA 3.1c defines user, virtual-environment, and operating-environment architecture in separate books; distinguish ISA instructions from platform requirements.

Arm provides machine-readable instruction/register/feature descriptions for A64 and A32/T32; use versioned XML/ASL and profile feature gates to populate encodings, operands, system effects, and pseudocode.

OpenPOWER's specification separates user, virtual-environment, and operating-environment instruction groups; a parsed JSON dataset is useful for indexing but should be cross-checked against the official versioned ISA.
Use the Intel SDM's A-Z instruction reference and Volume 4 MSR reference; implementation must gate by execution mode, CPUID feature, OS-enabled state, and processor generation.

Pin the unprivileged/privileged spec and extension versions independently; base, compressed, vector, atomic, CSR, and privilege instruction families need separate decode, semantics, and conformance states.

isa_inventory_policy.verification_rule: Instruction rows must be added only from a versioned authoritative reference or validated machine-readable definition. TableGen identifiers and family names are discovery candidates, not automatically architectural mnemonics or conformance evidence.

execution_model.policy: Discovery candidates are not conformance claims. Only explicitly implemented operations execute in the reference interpreter.

modes.native: Maps supported guest operations to Chimera semantic micro-ops; this is not native machine-code JIT output.
modes.compatibility: Interprets supported integer operations using deterministic reference semantics; unsupported operations fail closed.

raw.description: Raw instruction bytes; architecture and entry point must be supplied externally
